Author: @xanuviz
Content: It's hard to take a video like this seriously when the first "fact" is in fact a myth. The Piri Reis map doesn't show Antarctica but a distorted South America. The "ancient sources" mentioned are ancient Mediterranean geographic works, not some pre-historic civilization. There was also no USAF analysis of the map. That statement comes from a single source, Charles Hapgood’s 1966 book Maps of the Ancient Sea Kings, from a reply to a personal letter sent by Hapgood to a USAF officer. There was no official study or evaluation done by the USAF on this subject, the officer in question merely speculated based on what Hapgood told him. He was not a cartographer, not a geologist, nor part of any Antarctic research group.

I remember the cacophony of 35,000 mating pairs of penguins on one small island, not to mention the smell.  There were days where the weather would allow me to walk on the deck of the ship barefooted, wearing shorts and a t-shirt.  I drew an odd stare from one of the biologists so I just looked at him and said, "Because I can."

There is literally not a word in Antarctic Treaty about not letting people to go to Antarctic. There dozens of tourists going there. Anyone can go there. I facepalm every time someone tells that you can not go to Antarctica because of Antarctic Treaty.

The Antarctic Treaty was signed in Washington on 1 December 1959 by the twelve countries whose scientists had been active in and around Antarctica during the International Geophysical Year (IGY) of 1957-58. It entered into force in 1961 and has since been acceded to by many other nations. The total number of Parties to the Treaty is now 58.

Some important provisions of the Treaty:

Antarctica shall be used for peaceful purposes only
Art. I
Freedom of scientific investigation in Antarctica and cooperation toward that end… shall continue
Art. II
Scientific observations and results from Antarctica shall be exchanged and made freely available
Art. III
Among the signatories of the Treaty were seven countries - Argentina, Australia, Chile, France, New Zealand, Norway and the United Kingdom - with territorial claims , sometimes overlapping. Other countries do not recognize any claims. The US and Russia maintain a “basis of claim”. All positions are explicitly protected in Article IV, which preserves the status quo:

No acts or activities taking place while the present Treaty is in force shall constitute a basis for asserting, supporting or denying a claim to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica or create any rights of sovereignty in Antarctica. No new claim, or enlargement of an existing claim to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica shall be asserted while the present Treaty is in force.
To promote the objectives and ensure the observance of the provisions of the Treaty, "All areas of Antarctica, including all stations, installations and equipment within those areas … shall be open at all times to inspection " (Art. VII).

Author: @ralphralpherson9441
Content: Hate to break it to y'all, but the Piri Reis map shows South America and most of the Atlantic.  There is no "accurate to a few miles" coastline of Antarctica... however... it was common in those days to represent a theoretical southern continent they called "Terra Australis".... what the map actually shows is the South American coastline on the Atlantic, and down near Cape Horn, Piri Reis just sort of "made up" an incorrect rendering of South America merging into a mythical "lost continent" since ships of that era were not well suited to sail in Arctic seas.  The Vikings had small ships that could navigate in the Northern Seas... but not many folks were regularly sailing around Cape Horn until the early 1700s.  It was only discovered in 1616, so before then.... any map showing the southern tip of South America could only speculate what was down there.  You can strike that one off the "facts" list and add it to the "foil hat conspiracy" list.  Actual scholars have debunked the idea it shows Antarctica fairly soundly.

Author: @learnuiarchitecture
Content:
Yeah, you’re watching what’s basically a modern myth being rehashed with dramatic music.

Here’s the blunt truth:
	•	Antarctica wasn’t “locked down” in 1959. The Antarctic Treaty was signed that year to ban military activity and allow scientific cooperation. It’s open to peaceful research by over 50 countries.
	•	No, large parts aren’t blurred on Google Maps. What you’re seeing:
	•	Low-res satellite images due to poor weather and constant ice/snow cover.
	•	Clouds or compression artifacts, not censorship.
	•	Different map layers (terrain, satellite, etc.) showing inconsistencies, which gets misinterpreted.
	•	“They’re hiding something” is a trope. If there were alien bases or ancient pyramids, with today’s tech, drones, private satellites, and tens of thousands of scientists, someone credible would’ve leaked it by now.

Why the conspiracy persists:
	•	Antarctica is remote and mysterious.
	•	The treaty feels unusual to people unfamiliar with geopolitics.
	•	It’s an easy backdrop for sci-fi fantasies.

If you’re genuinely curious about Antarctica, look up the scientific bases, satellite missions like CryoSat-2, or check out HD footage from scientists stationed there. It’s stunning—no need for alien bunkers to make it fascinating.

Author: @harrisonm.2313
Content:
As someone who’s been to Antarctica, it is an incredible, amazing, vibrant place. It’s alien. And yes, it’s cold—though in summer not as cold as you think. It’s so much more alive than you’d think: I went on a research cruise for benthic population genomics, and the ocean bottom is covered in life—mostly brittle stars, but also sea stars, sponges, marine worms, shrimps, and cryonotothenoid fishes (there’s a species that has no hemoglobin in their blood, so their blood appears whitish-clear). In land, there’s SO MANY BIRDS—penguins, yes, but also sea birds like Wilson’s storm petrol, snow petrol, the skua. There’s all different kinds of seals, marine mammals, etc. There are NO land predators in Antarctica. Polar bears are Arctic! 
Antarctica is harsh, unforgiving. We had to complete a pretty rigorous physical qualification before going. It’s expensive—the ship we were on, the IVRB Nathaniel B Palmer (which has since been retired) has two engines. We used one. It cost about $100k a day to run, and there was only something like 74 people on the ship at the time.  

Antarctica is amazing. I wanna go back 😭 

5:45 to note, in that same study, much of the unknown archae they found was too contaminated to properly discern. No one wanted them to drill because they didn’t want to introduce a pollutant to the lake: the drill oil the Russians used did, in fact, pollute their water samples, so their entire study is basically too unreliable to take seriously. There’s a reason not many additional studies have been done on the water (at least, I don’t think—I haven’t looked in a while).

Author: @anthonym9494
Content:
Fact checked your first claim that the Piri Reis Maps display the Antarctic continent before it was originally discovered. To anyone interested in non-sensationalist dive into the reality of the Reis Maps. The area claimed to be Antarctica is more likely a distorted representation of South America.
	
Cartographic errors and lack of precise latitude/longitude knowledge in the 16th century make these kinds of distortions very common.
	
Antarctica was not discovered by Europeans until the 1820s, and no evidence suggests anyone mapped it before then.

The idea that it shows Antarctica without ice (which would mean over 6,000 years ago) is not supported by geology, archaeology, or mainstream history.

It’s more fun to speculate I guess but this is over-sensationalized media and not parallel to the true facts of the Reis Maps.

Author: @Strangeworkings
Content:
Love your videos, but for anyone who wants to know some additional context the pyramid formations appear geometric, but they are natural geological features and have been explanable for over 150 years. Geologists call them nunataks — peaks of mountains that protrude through ice sheets — shaped by glacial erosion, freezing and thawing, and wind. Similar examples: The Matterhorn in the Alps, Mount Assiniboine, Mount Thamserku  and many others. 
The pyramidal shape happens when three or more glaciers erode a mountain from different directions at roughly equal angles. Each glacier carves out a steep, U-shaped valley on its side of the mountain. Where those valleys meet, the remaining rock forms a sharp, pointed peak with flat triangular faces between the valleys.

Think of it like this:
Imagine three ice cream scoops taken out of a block from three sides — what’s left is a pointy peak with three faces.
If four glaciers carve from four directions, you get something like a four-sided pyramid, depending on how symmetrical the erosion is.

As to the largest base in Antartica, McMurdo Station. While it’s true that private defense contractors like Leidos or Raytheon have been heavily involved in managing logistics there, it’s a bit misleading to say the base is “owned” by them. It is the largest U.S. research facility in Antarctica, operated under the United States Antarctic Program (USAP). It’s located on Ross Island, and supports hundreds of scientists and logistical staff during the summer research season. It's not a military base, but a civilian scientific research station run by the National Science Foundation (NSF). Because of logistics and extreme conditions, the NSF outsources base operations to large companies with expertise in:
Remote logistics, Engineering, Infrastructure maintenance, Supply chains and airlift operations in dangerous environments.
These companies include:Raytheon Polar Services Company (until 2012), Lockheed Martin (2012–2016) Leidos (2016–present)
These companies aren’t running research or “owning” the base — they’re contracted to support it, much like private firms run infrastructure for NASA or the military.
